info.name: Sheria Platform API
info.description:
AI-powered judicial intelligence platform for Kenya's court system.

Provides agentic legal research, document verification, and predictive analytics via a streaming RAG pipeline.

## Auth
All protected endpoints require a `Bearer` JWT in the `Authorization` header.

Set the `jwt_token` collection variable to avoid repeating it per-request.

## Base URL
Set the `base_url` collection variable (default: `http://localhost:8000`).

variable.description: API base URL. Change for staging/production deployments.

item.name: Health
item.description: Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes. No authentication required.

request.description:
Always returns 200 OK while the server process is alive.

Kubernetes uses this probe to decide whether to **restart** the container. It performs no I/O.

Returns 200 when Redis and Neo4j are reachable; 503 when either dependency is down.

Kubernetes uses this probe to decide whether to **send traffic** to the pod.

item.name: Chat
item.description:
Streaming RAG pipeline endpoint. Responses are NDJSON (`application/x-ndjson`).

Each line is a JSON object with a `type` field:
- `"status"` — intermediate agent node completion event
- `"answer"` — final synthesised response from the Responder node
- `"error"` — unhandled exception during streaming

**Auth required:** Bearer JWT

exec: // Parse the first NDJSON line that contains session_id

request.description:
Starts a **new** conversation thread. Omit `session_id` to have the server generate one.

The response is an NDJSON stream. Each newline-delimited JSON object represents either an agent status update or the final answer.

The post-request test script automatically stores `session_id` in the collection variable for subsequent turns.

request.description:
Continues an existing conversation by supplying the `session_id` from a previous turn.

The server loads the last 6 message turns from Postgres to build the context window before running the agent.

item.name: Upload
item.description:
S3 presigned URL generation for direct client-to-S3 uploads.

**Flow:**
1. Call `POST /api/v1/upload/generate-presigned-url` → receive `upload_url`, `file_id`, `s3_key`
2. `PUT` the file binary directly to `upload_url` (client-side, no API proxy)
3. Pass `s3_key` to the ingestion pipeline

**Auth required:** Bearer JWT

request.description:
Generates a time-limited (1 hour) S3 presigned PUT URL.

The client uses the returned `upload_url` to upload the file binary directly to S3 without routing through the API server — suitable for large PDFs, court recordings, and exhibits.

The post-request test script saves `upload_url`, `file_id`, and `s3_key` as collection variables.

response.name: 500 Internal Server Error – S3 / IAM failure

header.description: Must match the content_type sent to generate-presigned-url

request.description:
Upload the binary file directly to S3 using the presigned URL obtained from the previous step.

**This request does NOT go through the Sheria API** — it goes directly to S3. No `Authorization` header is needed; the presigned URL is self-authenticating.

Set `upload_url` collection variable first by running "Generate Presigned Upload URL".

item.name: Feedback
item.description:
Rate individual assistant responses with a thumbs-up / thumbs-down score and an optional comment.

Feedback is persisted to the `feedback` table in PostgreSQL.

**Auth required:** Bearer JWT

request.description:
Submit a positive rating (`score: 1`) for an assistant response.

`message_id` is the primary-key ID of the `chat_history` row for the assistant's message.

response.name: 500 Internal Server Error – DB write failure

request.description:
Submit a negative rating (`score: -1`) with an optional explanatory comment.

Comments are used to improve the model via the judicial feedback loop (`eval/feedback/judicial_review.py`).
